h: Turning Edgbaston Into a Day Out
p: This part of south Birmingham is one of the city's leafiest corners, and the zoo is surrounded by good company. Cannon Hill Park, right on its doorstep, has a big boating lake, flower beds and plenty of play space, and the MAC, the Midlands Arts Centre, sits inside the park with a café, exhibitions and family events. Between them you've got an easy, budget-friendly afternoon that doesn't need much planning.

Not far away, the Birmingham Botanical Gardens in Edgbaston are a treat in any weather, with glasshouses full of tropical plants, desert cacti and Mediterranean shrubs, plus outdoor gardens and a play area. It's a natural next step for families who enjoyed the animals and want a bit more nature. Cricket fans will also know Edgbaston Stadium, the home of Warwickshire and a regular Test match ground, a short way up the road.
The River Rea runs alongside Cannon Hill Park, with a walking and cycling route that follows it through this part of the city. It's flat and pleasant, ideal for little bikes and scooters.

Practical tips: the zoo is small, so treat it as part of a bigger outing rather than a full-day trip in itself. Buses along the Pershore Road make it reachable without a car, which is handy given how busy Birmingham parking can be on a match day. Bring a ball and a blanket and let the park do the rest. Even on a grey day, the zoo, the park and the gardens together make for a relaxed, cheap and cheerful outing, and the city centre is only a short bus ride away for tea.
